Every economy as a multiple of world GNI: World Bank WDI, GNI per capita, Atlas method (NY.GNP.PCAP.CD) and population (SP.POP.TOTL); World Bank OGHIST (1 July 2026) for the operational thresholds; UN World Population Prospects 2024, medium variant; author's calculations and projections. Schellekens 2026, The Great Income Inversion, Moving Frontiers.
World GNI per capita is $14801 in 2026. The ratio column is each economy's GNI per capita divided by that.
Burundi at 0.016 times and Bermuda at 9.72 times span a 592-fold range.
Bubble area on the chart follows a logarithmic population scale; economies under ten million people are drawn at a fixed minimum size. The bubble_area column reproduces it.
Every person carries their own country's average, so these are measures of inequality between countries, not within them. A survey-based measure would be considerably wider.

Values from 2026 reflect a nowcast based on a conservative constant-pace scenario that replicates country-level median per capita income growth over the last decade. See Schellekens 2026 for methodology.
